Feed Environmental Footprint & Water Deprivation (AWARE / EF 3.1)

Water_and_Feed_Footprint.Rmd

1. Overview & Cradle-to-Farm-Gate Scope

In livestock life cycle assessment (LCA), on-farm direct emissions (Scope 1: enteric methane, manure management methane, and direct/indirect nitrous oxide) account for only part of the system’s total footprint. The production, processing, transport, and cultivation of animal feedstuffs represent a major upstream Scope 3 cradle-to-farm-gate environmental burden.

herdr couples animal nutrition—specifically animal Dry Matter Intake (DMI) and dietary ingredient proportions—with international life cycle inventories:

  • INRAE / ADEME ECOALIM v9 & AGRIBALYSE v3.1: Life cycle inventories for animal feed raw materials under the European Commission EF 3.1 (PEF) framework. Because these are process LCA datasets, upstream economic allocation for co-products (e.g., oilseed meals, cereal brans) is already resolved at the processing gate.
  • European Commission Environmental Footprint (EF 3.1): Methodological package adopted under Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 for Product Environmental Footprint (PEF).

The model evaluates three primary environmental dimensions for feedstuffs:

  1. Carbon Footprint (GHG): Differentiating between fossil inputs (CO2e\text{CO}_2\text{e} from machinery, synthetic fertilizers, electricity) and land-use change / deforestation (CO2e\text{CO}_2\text{e} from LUC, particularly critical in imported soybean meal).
  2. Agricultural Land Footprint: Partitioned into agroecological soil classifications (cropland, convertible grassland, unconvertible rangeland) following Mottet et al. (2017).
  3. Water Deprivation Footprint: Freshwater deprivation characterized with the international AWARE model.

2. Calculation Methodology: Step-by-Step

In herdr, calculating feed environmental footprints (both Water Deprivation and Greenhouse Gas emissions) follows a 3-step pipeline:

2.1 Annual Ingredient Dry Matter Intake

How much of ingredient ii an animal consumes over a year depends on daily dry matter intake (DMIkg/dayDMI_{\text{kg/day}}), the broad feed category share (Sharecat∈{forage,concentrate,milk,milk_replacer}Share_{cat} \in \{\text{forage}, \text{concentrate}, \text{milk}, \text{milk\_replacer}\} from diet_profiles.csv), and the specific ingredient’s share within that category (ShareiShare_i from diet_ingredients.csv):

AnnualDMIi(kg DM / head / yr)=(DMIkg/day×365)×(Sharecat100)×(Sharei100) AnnualDMI_i \; (\text{kg DM / head / yr}) = (DMI_{\text{kg/day}} \times 365) \times \left(\frac{Share_{cat}}{100}\right) \times \left(\frac{Share_i}{100}\right)

2.2 Conversion to As-Fed Fresh Weight

Because Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) emission factors in ECOALIM v9 / AGRIBALYSE v3.1 are expressed per kilogram of fresh feedstuff as fed (rather than 100% dry matter), herdr converts dry matter intake to as-fed fresh weight using the ingredient’s dry matter percentage (DM_pctiDM\_pct_i) from feed_characteristics.csv:

AnnualFreshi(kg fresh / head / yr)=AnnualDMIi(DM_pcti100) AnnualFresh_i \; (\text{kg fresh / head / yr}) = \frac{AnnualDMI_i}{\left(\frac{DM\_pct_i}{100}\right)}

(If DM_pctiDM\_pct_i is missing or non-positive, herdr defaults to 100%).

2.3 Individual and Herd Footprints

Environmental impacts are calculated by multiplying the annual fresh feed consumed by the corresponding characterization factor (EFiEF_i) from ecoalim.parquet:

Water Deprivation Footprint (m3 depriv.m^3\text{ depriv.})

WaterPerAnimali(m3 depriv. / head / yr)=AnnualFreshi×EFwater,i WaterPerAnimal_i \; (\text{m}^3\text{ depriv. / head / yr}) = AnnualFresh_i \times EF_{water, i}

TotalWateri(m3 depriv. / herd / yr)=WaterPerAnimali×Population TotalWater_i \; (\text{m}^3\text{ depriv. / herd / yr}) = WaterPerAnimal_i \times Population

where EFwater,iEF_{water, i} is Water use (m3 depriv.) based on the AWARE characterization model.

Feed Greenhouse Gas Emissions (kg CO2e\text{kg CO}_2\text{e})

GHGPerAnimali(kg CO2e / head / yr)=AnnualFreshi×EFclimate,i GHGPerAnimal_i \; (\text{kg CO}_2\text{e / head / yr}) = AnnualFresh_i \times EF_{climate, i}

TotalGHGi(kg CO2e / herd / yr)=GHGPerAnimali×Population TotalGHG_i \; (\text{kg CO}_2\text{e / herd / yr}) = GHGPerAnimal_i \times Population

where EFclimate,iEF_{climate, i} corresponds to the total (Climate change - EF 3.1), fossil (Climate change - Fossil), or land-use change / deforestation (Climate change - Land use and LU change) characterization factor.

3. Water Deprivation (AWARE Model): Physical Volume vs. Scarcity

A common source of confusion in livestock environmental reporting is equating the Water Deprivation Footprint with physical cubic meters (m3m^3) of water pumped, drank, or evaporated on the farm:

  • Scarcity-weighted, not volumetric: The indicator does not measure raw physical gallons or m3m^3 of water extracted from a well. It quantifies potential freshwater deprivation relative to the world consumption-weighted average (m3 depriv.m^3\text{ depriv.} or m3 world-eq.m^3\text{ world-eq.}) using characterization factors from the European Commission’s Environmental Footprint (EF 3.1) and the AWARE (Available WAter REmaining) model (Boulay et al., 2018; UNEP-SETAC WULCA working group).
  • For the complete hydrological model and watershed equations, see the primary reference: Boulay et al. (2018).

4. Feed Carbon Footprint Breakdown: Fossil vs. LUC

In addition to water, herdr evaluates feed greenhouse gas emissions across two distinct life cycle mechanisms:

  1. Fossil & Inputs GHG (CO2efossil\text{CO}_2\text{e}_{\text{fossil}}):
    • Emissions stemming from mineral fertilizer synthesis (Haber-Bosch process for nitrogen), agrochemical manufacturing, tractor diesel during tillage and harvesting, natural gas for grain and forage dehydration, and grid electricity.
  2. Land-Use Change / Deforestation GHG (CO2eluc\text{CO}_2\text{e}_{\text{luc}}):
    • Direct greenhouse gas releases associated with deforestation and conversion of native biomes (e.g., Amazon, Cerrado, Chaco) to agricultural cropland within a 20-year retrospective horizon.
    • Particularly dominant in feed rations relying on solvent-extracted soybean meal imported from South American origins without zero-deforestation certification.

5. R Code Workflow

5.1 Evaluating Standalone Feed Footprints

The calculate_feed_emissions() function can be run directly on any scenario directory containing user_data/:

library(herdr)

# 1. Run standalone feed footprint calculation
feed_results <- calculate_feed_emissions(
  data_dir = system.file("Examples/Level1_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015", package = "herdr"),
  saveoutput = FALSE
)

# Preview columns
head(feed_results[, c(
  "animal_tag", "population",
  "feed_CO2e_fossil_kg_year", "feed_CO2e_luc_kg_year",
  "feed_water_m3_year", "feed_water_per_head_year"
)])

5.2 Full Cradle-to-Farm-Gate Impact Assessment

The complete pipeline generate_impact_assessment() merges animal biology, IPCC Tier 2 direct emissions, Mottet land competition, and feed life cycle footprints:

# 2. Run consolidated impact assessment
impact_results <- generate_impact_assessment(
  data_dir = system.file("Examples/Level1_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015", package = "herdr"),
  saveoutput = FALSE,
  ar = "AR5"
)

5.3 Visualizing Water and Feed Footprints

Use plot_herdr_results() with standardized selectors:

# A) Dedicated Water Deprivation Footprint (Total herd, in Mm3 depriv.)
p_water_total <- plot_herdr_results(
  df = impact_results,
  group_cols = "animal_tag",
  impact_category = "water",
  functional_unit = "total"
)
p_water_total

# B) Water Deprivation Intensity per kg of Milk (in m3 depriv. / kg FPCM milk)
p_water_milk <- plot_herdr_results(
  df = impact_results,
  group_cols = "animal_tag",
  impact_category = "water",
  functional_unit = "milk"
)
p_water_milk

# C) Multi-Impact Overview (Carbon, Land, Water in a 3-panel comparison)
p_overview <- plot_herdr_results(
  df = impact_results,
  group_cols = "animal_tag",
  impact_category = "overview"
)
p_overview
